sessionTitle: Shipping custom models at scale from fine-tuning to inference

announcements.name: Fireworks AI is available on Microsoft Azure
announcements.shortDescription: Ferguson notes the managed inference and training service, highlighted in Build announcements, can now be used on Azure.
announcements.longDescription: Rob Ferguson, VP of Technology at Fireworks AI, introduces Fireworks as a managed service providing both AI inference performance and AI training. He notes the announcements made at Build and highlights that the service can now be used on Microsoft Azure.

announcements.name: Unsloth has reached 300 million total downloads on Hugging Face
announcements.shortDescription: Han cites the milestone while describing Unsloth's work fixing model bugs and speeding up training.
announcements.longDescription: Daniel Han from Unsloth [inferred] describes how the team helps large labs release models and fixes bugs in them, noting they just reached 300 million total downloads on Hugging Face. He mentions Unsloth makes training faster and more memory efficient, also supports reinforcement learning, has a GitHub package, and offers a UI.

announcements.name: Unsloth–Thinking Machines collaboration on LoRA
announcements.shortDescription: Han references a joint blog post ("LoRA Without Regret" [inferred]) showing that even a LoRA rank of 1 works well for specific use cases like math and coding.
announcements.longDescription: Daniel Han explains LoRA as a fine-tuning approach where, instead of updating every weight, you add a small sliver of weights (an A matrix times a B matrix) added to the large model, updating only about 1% of weights for much less memory usage. He references a collaboration with Thinking Machines on a blog post ("LoRA Without Regret" [inferred]) showing that even a LoRA rank of 1 works well for specific use cases like math and coding. He cautions that hyperparameters must be chosen carefully, such as a learning rate 10 times larger than normal (2E-4) and an adjusted alpha/scaling.
